original_question: For each positive integer n, what is the smallest triangle that can contain n circles of radius 1 without overlap?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4 ("Erdös-Oler packaging problem"): the general question of packing n unit circles into an arbitrary triangle of minimum size, rather than the narrower equilateral-triangle subcase. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's main quantifier (for each positive integer n), the objects being packed (circles of radius 1), and the basic optimization goal (the smallest triangle containing them without overlap). In substance, it is very close to the paper's official Problem 4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))
missing_details: The paper's verb is "package": the circles must be completely contained in the triangle, not merely have their centers inside it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))

"Smallest triangle" should be made explicit as a triangle of minimum area; otherwise the optimization criterion is ambiguous for noncongruent triangles. This is a sharpening needed to make the question fully stand-alone, even though the paper itself uses the informal word "smallest." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))

The optimization ranges over all triangles in the Euclidean plane, not only equilateral triangles; the paper treats the equilateral case separately as a narrower "Particular case of Problem 4." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))

"Without overlap" should be formalized as pairwise interior-disjoint unit disks, so tangency is allowed. This matches the paper's earlier overlap convention for plane bodies. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))

A fully stand-alone formulation should say explicitly whether the goal is to determine the extremal triangle itself, the minimum possible area, or both; the paper's phrase "find the smallest triangle" suggests the triangle up to congruence, while a research question is sharper if the extremal quantity is stated. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))
refined_question: For each positive integer n, determine a triangle T in the Euclidean plane of minimum area among all triangles that can contain n closed disks of radius 1 with pairwise disjoint interiors; equivalently, each of the n unit circles must lie completely inside T, and the circles may touch each other or the boundary of T but may not overlap. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))
justification: This paper is a short list of open plane-geometry problems and does not contain a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. Your draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 4, Problem 4. The only nearby narrower statement is the "Particular case of Problem 4," which adds equilateral-triangle and triangular-number hypotheses; since your draft does not mention those extra restrictions, the nearest paper-faithful target is the general Problem 4, not that subcase. The main refinements needed are to spell out containment, the meaning of non-overlap, and the optimization criterion behind "smallest." No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic qualifiers are relevant here because the target problem is purely Euclidean-geometric. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2104.09324))
